To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Update and Disclosure Letter

## Threshold caution: reject the framing before the substance

Before any clause, the package is built on a set of assertions designed to shut down review, and none survives our own authority process (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3):

- **"[STANDARD] … reviewed and cleared by both sides … need no further scrutiny"** — I have no record of any such clearance, and a counterparty's label is not our authority. Every "[STANDARD]" item below is in fact a *departure* from our baseline. The tag is doing the opposite of what it claims.
- **"settled at principal level … reflect the agreed commercial bargain … marked FINAL"** — nothing confirms Amelia Frost (or any buyer principal) agreed these. "Final" and "agreed" are not self-proving.
- **"10–20% caps / ~1% baskets / 12–18 months … standard and widely accepted market terms"** — a "market standard" assertion is not binding and not evidence. We negotiate to our playbook, not to the seller's description of the market.

So I'm treating the whole package as the other side's opening draft, and reviewing all of it.

## Material departures from our playbook

**1. General liability cap — Cl 12.1 (AUD 4,800,000 / 20%)**
Our starting position is 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure matches our *conditional fallback* — but the playbook is explicit: a fallback is not cleared merely because a number matches it, and 20% requires **prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft**, which has not been given. Push back to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do **not** concede 20% on the basis that the seller already wrote it in.

**2. Thresholds — Cl 12.2**
Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery. Our playbook: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once the basket is exceeded. Three separate departures — the de minimis is 5x, the basket is 5x, and the "excess above the basket" mechanic directly contradicts our first-dollar position. Push back on all three.

**3. Time limits — Cl 12.3/13 (18 months)**
Our baseline is 24 months; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval (none given). Same trap as the cap. Also reject the sweep-up "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" — that silently drags Fundamental/Title/Tax into the general regime (see 4 and 10).

**4. Fundamental / Title collapsed into the general regime**
Seller wants capacity and title warranties under the "same caps and time limits … for administrative simplicity." This is the single most dangerous move in the draft. Our playbook requires a **separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.** Reject outright. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title recovery at 20% for 18 months.

**5. Fraud carve-out — missing**
The draft contains Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 (limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature") but **no carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct.** Our playbook requires these carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and says no one may waive this. Insist on the carve-out and ensure "all Claims of any nature" is made expressly subject to it.

**6. Buyer-knowledge exclusion — Cl 8.3**
Blanket bar on any matter the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge" including "anything discoverable from the data room or public records." Delete. Our playbook deletes blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs **named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry**, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. Note this exclusion is especially pernicious combined with the whole-data-room disclosure in item 7 — together they would gut nearly every warranty.

**7. Disclosure — Sch 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1], [1.2]**
Deemed disclosure of the **entire indexed data room (DD-002–DD-012)**, the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." Reject. Our playbook requires **specific fair disclosure** and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. [1.4]'s "nothing admits… that any consent/payment/notice is legally required" is a standard reservation — acceptable as a reservation, but it does not cure the deemed-disclosure defect.

**8. Bluefen consent — Cl 3/6.3**
Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and "consent satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." The Disclosure Letter item 2 confirms there is **no final consent and no evidence conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue — a material customer. Our playbook requires **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**, not consent-on-delivery, and says reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent. Make effective, condition-satisfied consent a Completion condition.

**9. Riverlark — Cl 2/7**
Seller offers a release "following Completion." Disclosure item 3 confirms ~AUD 3,200,000 is unpaid with no discharge. Our playbook requires a **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.** A post-completion release is only acceptable with an **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** (not obtained). Push for direct repayment and release at Completion. (Note the seller letter says "approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding" — confirm the current payout figure; the ~3.2m is a round number, not a verified payout.)

**10. Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000)**
Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" and deliberately **not itemised in the funds flow.** That is exactly the silent exclusion our playbook forbids. Require them as a **specific line item or seller-funded**, and note Disclosure item 5 confirms **on-costs (payroll tax, super) are unquantified** — the triggered on-costs must also be captured, not just the headline AUD 420,000.

**11. Ironquay IP — Cl 11.1 (AUD 180,000)**
Seller calls the SOW3-limited indemnity "adequate." Our playbook says **broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure.** Disclosure item 4 is important: DD-010's AUD 180,000 is "not independent bank verification of non-payment," and there's no receipt or confirmatory assignment. So the AUD 180,000 is **not verified either way** — do not accept it as settled, and do not assume non-payment either. Broaden the indemnity; keep the SOW3 cure (transfer on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees).

**12. Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
Seller frames it as "preliminary… not material." Disclosure item 6 is more accurate: ~1,240 records possibly exported, but **no confirmed unauthorised access, no confirmed scope, no confirmed notification duty, no loss amount.** Correct posture per playbook: **assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction**; require log preservation, continued investigation, and status updates. Don't accept "not material" as a conclusion, and don't overclaim a breach.

**13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
Seller labels them "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure item 8 admits the record **doesn't say** whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. Our playbook: **assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction** — but equally, do not accept automatic "ordinary course" write-off. Request the underlying terms to characterise them.

**14. Tax / IP — "settled under the general regime"**
These remain **OPEN** per our playbook — assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. Reject the seller's attempt to fold them into (and cap them under) the general regime. Keep Tax/IP/Title/payment/covenant categories separate with no hidden general-regime override (this links back to the Cl 13 sweep-up in item 3).

**15. Title evidence — Disclosure item 10 / DD-012**
Seller relies solely on the DD-012 share register. Our playbook: DD-012 is a **supplied internal source, not independent proof.** Require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence (e.g. independent register search, directors'/company confirmations, encumbrance checks). Helpfully, Disclosure item 10 itself concedes DD-012 "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification."

**16. Minor items to note (not adverse but confirm):** Office lease (item 7) and Mossvale (item 9) — the disclosures state neither requires consent *merely because shares are sold*. Acceptable as drafted, but verify against the actual DD-007/DD-009 clauses rather than relying on the characterisation.

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our push-back |
|---|-------|-----------------|---------------|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | 25% / 6.0m; 20% needs Frost written authority (none) |
| 2 | Thresholds | DM 25k / basket 250k / excess-only | DM 5k / basket 50k / first-dollar |
| 3 | Time limit | 18 months + sweep-up | 24 months; delete "applies to all Claims" sweep-up |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | Separate regime: 100%, ≥6 yrs, outside basket/DM/knowledge |
| 5 | Fraud | No carve-out | Carve fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct out of all caps/baskets/limits/exclusive remedy/non-reliance |
| 6 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket + "discoverable" bar | Delete; at most named persons + reasonable enquiry; never title/capacity/fraud/specific indemnity |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | Specific fair disclosure only |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours / consent-on-delivery | Effective + condition-satisfied consent as Completion condition |
| 9 | Riverlark | Release after Completion | Current payout + direct repayment + release at Completion |
| 10 | Bonuses | Not itemised, "seller's matter" | Specific line item or seller-funded; capture on-costs |
| 11 | Ironquay | SOW3-only, "adequate", 180k | Broaden indemnity, keep SOW3 cure; 180k unverified |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | No conclusion either way; preserve logs, investigate, update |
| 13 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | Assess on terms; no automatic classification |
| 14 | Tax/IP | Settled under general regime | OPEN; separate; no unlimited liability, no resolution |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent title/encumbrance/authority evidence |

**Overarching points to make to the seller:** (1) We do not accept the "[STANDARD]/FINAL/agreed/market" framing — none of these positions is cleared on our side, and several (20% cap, 18 months) only superficially resemble our fallbacks, which require specific written authority we have not given. (2) The most structurally dangerous moves are the collapse of Fundamental/Title into the general regime (item 4), the absence of a fraud carve-out (item 5), and the combination of whole-data-room disclosure plus a blanket buyer-knowledge bar (items 6–7), which together would hollow out the warranty package. Those four should be our priority asks.

Two confirmations I'd flag for the deal team rather than decide myself: the exact current Riverlark payout figure (the "~3.2m" is a round estimate), and whether anyone will represent that Amelia Frost has in fact authorised the 20% cap or 18-month period — my working assumption, absent any such authority in the record, is that she has not.

Want me to draft the mark-up / issues list in a form you can send to the seller?
